text:
Nikita Kucherov asked the Lightning for a trade at the end of October, telling reporters it was about poor communication and respect, not money, per NHL.com. GM Julien BriseBois said the team has no intention of trading him, and he's still here, still scoring: a hat trick against Buffalo last weekend. That tension sits over everything Tampa Bay does this season.

So far it hasn't hurt them. The Lightning are 14-5-2 with 30 points and the chances back it: 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 56% at five on five. That's a good team, not a lucky one. Kucherov, Jake Guentzel and Brayden Point have outscored opponents 10-2 at 62%, and Point is back after Daily Faceoff reported his activation from injured reserve. The checking line of Zemgus Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev has been a quiet weapon at 11-5, though Girgensons left Tuesday's game with an injury.

The blue line is producing more than it should. John Carlson, in his first season in Tampa, has 14 points in his last ten games against 7.5 expected, and Erik Cernak six against 2.8. Both are running well ahead of their chances. Rookie Sam O'Reilly scored his first NHL goal against Washington. Our numbers make Jon Cooper's team 96% to make the playoffs. The question is whether Kucherov is still part of it in March.
